severityNote: Proposed HIGH; FLAGGED FOR SEVERITY REVIEW (High vs Medium). High if a zero/near-zero-price dispatcher is registerable (theft of entire pot for ~0 cost); at minimum Medium where the async-funded pot drifts above nudgeSize x cheapest-price, making the drain net-profitable.
title: Incomplete fix: value-blind nudge gate lets attacker drain the entire nudge pot via a caller-chosen cheap/zero-price dispatcher
description: batchMint pays out the contract's ENTIRE nudgePaymentToken balance whenever the purely-numeric gate count >= nudgeSize is met (gate at line 215, full-balance payout at lines 219-224). The payout amount is decoupled from the value actually paid by the caller, and dispatcherIndex (line 186) is fully caller-controlled. The recent fix (NatSpec lines 17-29) pinned the minter to close the prior 'no-op minter' drain, but its own stated security goal -- 'qualifying for the nudge now requires genuinely paying for >= nudgeSize real mints at the dispatcher's ramping price' -- fails: the attacker simply selects the cheapest registered dispatcher index to clear the gate. The mint loop at lines 207-209 calls nftMinter.mint(dispatcherIndex, recipient) count times against that caller-chosen index.
impact: Theft of the entire externally-funded nudge pot (e.g. USDC routed in from the yield funnel) by any caller for ~0 cost (zero-price dispatcher) or sub-pot cost (cheapest normal-priced dispatcher once the async-funded pot has drifted above nudgeSize x cheapest-price). This is the same exploit class the fix claimed to close.
attackPath: Attacker observes a funded nudgePaymentToken balance on BatchNFTMinter (async-funded from the yield funnel).

Attacker identifies the cheapest registered, non-disabled dispatcher index in the sibling NFTMinterV2. Confirmed cross-contract precondition: NFTMinterV2.registerDispatcher (~lines 125-147) and setPrice (~line 282) enforce NO price > 0 validation, so a zero/near-zero-price dispatcher (prime token != nudgeToken) is registerable; mint(index, recipient) (~line 159) is permissionless for any registered, non-disabled index.

Attacker calls batchMint(paymentToken, cheapDispatcherIndex, count=nudgeSize, recipient=attacker, paymentAmount~=0). The up-front guard at line 200 only blocks nudgePaymentToken == paymentToken, which the attacker avoids by choosing a different prime token.
The loop performs nudgeSize real mints at ~0 (paymentAmount=0) cost.
The numeric gate count >= nudgeSize at line 215 is satisfied; line 220 reads the full live balanceOf and line 222 transfers the ENTIRE nudge pot to the attacker-controlled recipient.
Even with only normal-priced dispatchers available, whenever the pot exceeds nudgeSize x cheapest-price the drain is net-profitable.
recommendation: Make the nudge payout value-aware rather than purely count-gated. Options: (1) gate the nudge on cumulative value actually paid (totalPaid) at/above a threshold rather than on count alone; (2) restrict eligible dispatcher indices to an owner-curated allowlist with enforced minimum price; (3) cap the nudge payout per call to a fixed/derived amount rather than sweeping the full balance; (4) require the sibling NFTMinterV2 to enforce price > 0 in registerDispatcher/setPrice (cross-submodule change -- coordinate via the interface-change flow). A coded PoC is required before report generation to confirm the zero-price registration path and the full-pot sweep end-to-end.

preconditions: mint(index, recipient) (~159): permissionless for any registered non-disabled index
crossContract.verified: Sibling file present at lib/yield-claim-nft/src/V2/NFTMinterV2.sol; precondition per scan/econ scratch and task narrative.
